name: Dargwa
notes: Dargwa (дарган мез), Northeast Caucasian (Dargic) macro-language of central Dagestan; the literary standard is based on the Akusha dialect and has used a Cyrillic alphabet with the Dagestani ⟨ъ⟩/⟨ь⟩/palochka-style ejective marking since 1938. SKELETON: grapheme inventory now specified. The plain stop/affricate series п/т/ц/ч is phonetically ASPIRATED [pʰ tʰ t͡sʰ t͡ʃʰ], contrasting with a geminate/fortis (tense) series spelled with doubled letters (пп/тт/цц/чч) and a glottalised (ejective) series marked with the palochka digraph (кӏ тӏ цӏ чӏ лӏ), following the three-way laryngeal system described for Dargic by van den Berg (2001) and Sumbatova & Mutalov (2003) for the closely related Icari dialect — the same three-way pattern (plain aspirated / tense / ejective) that the Avar (`av`) and Lezgian (`lez`) Dagestani specs already encode for their own stop series, adapted here to Dargwa's own inventory rather than copied wholesale (a shared alphabet convention is not a shared phonology: see AGENTS.md). Uvular ⟨хъ⟩ is analysed as a plain uvular stop /q/ (contrasting with pharyngealised ⟨хӏ⟩ /ħ/ and uvular fricative ⟨х⟩ /χ/) per the standard Akusha consonant chart. Dargic dialects vary substantially (Dargwa is sometimes treated as a language cluster rather than one language); this spec targets the literary Akusha-based standard only. STRESS EXEMPTION: Dargwa word stress is not consistently orthography-predictable across dialects and is not asserted here; no `stress` block is declared.
